GAF Master Elite® — the credential behind the warranty

Master Elite® is GAF's top-tier factory certification for residential roofing contractors. It is not a badge a contractor can buy — it is earned against GAF's standards for licensing, insurance, reputation, and installation training, and it has to be maintained.

It matters for one practical reason: only certified contractors can offer GAF's strongest warranty options. Golden Key's advertised 50-year warranty and its Master Elite® status are the same story told twice — once as a credential, once as a guarantee.

  • Factory-certified by GAF, North America's largest roofing manufacturer
  • Held to ongoing standards for workmanship and homeowner satisfaction

Before you turn the key

What does the 50-year warranty cover?+

Golden Key advertises a 50-year warranty on its roofing work. The exact coverage, terms, and what registration involves are confirmed in writing with your free estimate, before any work begins — ask for the full terms and keep them with your house paperwork.

What is a GAF Master Elite® contractor?+

It is GAF's top factory certification for residential roofers, earned against standards for licensing, insurance, reputation, and installation training. Only Master Elite® contractors can offer GAF's strongest warranty options — which is how a 50-year advertised warranty is possible.

Is the estimate really free?+

Yes. The estimate — including the on-site look, measurements, and your written options — is free, with no obligation to book the work.

Why add photos to the form?+

Photos of the roof, the damage, and the problem areas let the team arrive at your callback already knowing what they're looking at — a faster, sharper estimate. Your photos stay on your device; attach them in your email app when you send the summary.

Which areas do you serve?+

Golden Key Construction Group is based on Staten Island and serves Staten Island homeowners. If you're just off the island, send the form anyway — coverage is confirmed when the team calls back.

Repair or full replacement — how do I know?+

That's what the inspection is for. Curling, cracked, or missing shingles and recurring leaks point one way; isolated storm damage points the other. The estimate spells out both options honestly when both are viable.
